title: Large Rockfall at Halema`uma`u Crater
place: Overlook-crater lava lake, Halemaʻumaʻu, Kīlauea summit, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
notes: Night webcam (grayscale, high contrast) on the crater rim looking into the lava lake; time-lapse-like (frames seconds apart, played at 15 fps source, duplicated to 30). 0-1.9 s: calm lake, black crust plates with glowing cracks (bowl x~0.1-0.95,y~0.15-0.85). 2.0 s: rockfall at right hits the lake and the lake explodes - spatter cloud upper-right (x~0.75,y~0.3). 2.5-3.5 s: incandescent fragments fly at the camera, streaks fill the whole frame, glowing bits land on the rim (bottom-left). 3.5-4.5 s: frame washed out by glow. 4.5-12 s: lake reappears torn open - bright white churning lava lower right (x~0.7,y~0.7), new crack pattern. Webcam timestamp text at the very top (y<0.04, x<0.35) - crop/trim the top. Source 1296x960 (4:3) 15 fps -> 1458x1080, 30 fps. Best shot A 0.0-2.4 (calm cracked lake -> blast starts at 2.0); shot B 2.0-4.6 (explosion, fragments fly at camera); shot C 5.0-7.6 (lake torn open, glowing). Grayscale - no orange.
fact_en: This morning's event was vigorous enough to hurl incandescent fragments onto the rim of Halema‘uma‘u Crater, about 110 m (360 ft) above the lava lake surface. This Quicktime movie shows some of these fragments flying toward the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory webcam that is perched on the rim of the crater.
